steps: Form a flat hand with your dominant hand, fingers pressed together and the thumb resting along the side.
Bring the hand up to the side of your head, near your cheek or temple.
Rest the side of your head against the hand, tilting slightly as if settling onto a pillow.
Keep the palm facing toward your face with the fingers pointing toward your ear.
Hold the position briefly with a relaxed face, as if you are ready to fall asleep.
tip: Use this sign only for the thing you sleep on — for a truck bed or a flower bed, fingerspell B-E-D.

steps: Raise your dominant hand to about shoulder height to begin signing a number.
Hold up one through five fingers for an isolated number, with your palm facing back toward you.
Roll the wrist as you twist from six through ten, keeping the motion small and even.
Turn your palm forward when the number is part of a series, such as a phone number or address.
For a multi-digit number, show the first digit and then the second in quick succession with the same hand.
Keep a neutral face; emphasis comes from the hand position, not from facial expression.
tip: Isolated numbers go palm-back (the least tiring wrist position); sequences, ages, and times go palm-forward.

steps: Spell T with your dominant hand, the thumb resting against the folded index finger.
Shift into a modified O handshape, using only your thumb, index, and middle fingers in a loose ring.
Slide the hand about two inches to the side while the handshape rounds out.
Finish with the L handshape, index finger pointing up and thumb stretched outward.
Keep your palm angled forward toward your conversation partner through the whole movement.
Mouth the word tool naturally while spelling, instead of naming each letter aloud.
tip: TOOL has no widely accepted sign — Deaf signers fingerspell it, blended into one quick, sign-like unit.

steps: Raise both hands in front of your chest with index fingers extended and the other fingers closed.
Point the two index fingers toward each other in the space before your chest.
Rotate both index fingers around one another in small, even circles.
Move both hands toward your body as the fingers circle, pulling the motion inward.
Keep your palms facing roughly inward, the fingertips gliding past each other without touching.
Tilt your head slightly forward with raised eyebrows, as if inviting the person closer.
tip: COME is uninflected — the same production covers come, comes, and coming; direction shows who is moving.
